name: Clamps bound the worst public error at apply
non_visual_rationale: The observables are the published effective height and the published integer score, plus the bytes still sitting at the correction key after the build. No template, string or style is touched. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
why_no_production_change: Both clamps were delivered by 02-02 and already bind at apply: storedScoreMoveOf saturates the score move at the record's OWN clamp.max_abs_score, and storedMemberHeightMoveOf saturates each member's move at the record's OWN max_abs_h_frac of that member's raw height, which is why build.ts passes the raw height in. This step proves both bind on the number a surfer actually reads, and that the file is not rewritten to fit them. Nothing under src/ was touched; `git diff --stat src/` is deliberately empty.
criteria_delivered: 1. A passing record ordering a 2.0 m height move changes the published height by at most forty percent of the forecast. The record orders 2.0 m against members 1.20 m to 1.26 m tall; the published effective height falls from 1.531337650552614 m to 0.9188025903315684 m, which is exactly the 0.4 the record itself states and not a metre more. Asserted both ways: at most the bound, and all the way TO the bound, because a body that moved less would pass a one-sided check while the clamp was not what stopped it.

2. A passing record ordering a 30-point score move changes the published score by at most twelve points. It falls 91 to 79, exactly the 12 the record states. The archived bias_applied is -0.12, the CLAMPED move rather than the ordered one, so an operator reads what was applied rather than what was asked for. The fixture isolates the score lane on purpose: its height key states a difference of zero and is refused on its own significance rung, so the published wave is untouched and the score clamp is the only thing that can bound the move. Both facts are asserted, not assumed.

3. Both clamps bind at APPLY time in the builder and the stored file is never rewritten to fit them. Each example asserts the bytes at the spot's correction key are byte-identical to the record written before the build. The assertion is load-bearing, not decorative: a mutation that made the build normalise the file to its clamps failed both examples on exactly that line.
scope_note: The accepted roadmap names src/scoring/engine.ts and tests/unit/learning-apply-recheck.test.ts. engine.ts already carries both clamps, delivered under 02-02 with its own generated saturation and exactness laws, and editing it here to satisfy a file list would be manufacturing a diff. learning-apply-recheck.test.ts already quantifies both clamps over their whole generated space with max_abs_h_frac and max_abs_score GENERATED rather than pinned, so a body that hardcoded 0.40 or 12 is already caught there. What that file cannot see is whether a bounded move reaches a published number, which is this step's whole claim and is an acceptance-level one.
acceptance: Two examples through runBuildOnce, one per clamp, each carrying the file-not-rewritten assertion. Each carries a non-vacuity guard that fails the example outright if the fixture does not genuinely order MORE than the bound allows -- for height, more than forty percent of the TALLEST member, so no member escapes the test; for score, more than the twelve points stated. The score example additionally asserts the day-zero score has room to fall the whole twelve, so the floor at zero can never be what stopped the move instead of the clamp.
fixture_arithmetic: Measured against the real emitter before the assertions were written. Height: a forecast 2.0 m above the reported band's midpoint yields a height key of b exactly 2.0 m on the physical-floor error alone, clearing its ladder by better than thirty times. Every member is bounded at 0.4 of its own height, so each corrected member is exactly 0.6 of its raw height, the blend is 0.6 of the day-zero blend, and the published effective height -- a fixed positive multiple of the blended height while the period is unchanged -- falls by exactly the allowed fraction. Score: a shown score of 100 against a reported quality worth 70 yields a score key of b 30.0 points, and the same fixture's forecast sits exactly on the reported band's midpoint so its height key states 0 and is refused. That refusal is what isolates the score lane.
test_budget: Two behaviours: a height order past the bound is bounded at the published wave; a score order past the limit is bounded at the published score. Budget 2 x 2 = 4. Delivered 2 acceptance examples. The file-not-rewritten claim is folded into both rather than given a third example, because it is a property of the same two builds and a separate example would run them again to assert one more line.
unit_law: NONE ADDED. 02-02's four fast-check laws already quantify both clamps over generated records with both limits generated, including a counter that fails the law outright if the generated space contained no draw where the clamp could bind. Mirroring them here would restate a proven claim at a layer that adds nothing.
red_evidence: No production code changes under this step, so RED was taken against the SHIPPED body by controlled mutation, each planted alone, each reverted, typecheck clean under every one, zero collection errors. (1) G5's bound REMOVED entirely (`return stated.b`): the height example fails, but on the harness precondition -- 'the fixture must publish before anything about it can be read; got published:false, missing complete today or tomorrow ranking'. That is worth recording rather than hiding: an unclamped 2.0 m move drives every member of a 1.2 m morning below zero, blend finds no usable member and the build refuses to publish at all. It is a red, and it is also a statement about how far past the honest range an unbounded file can push this product. (2) Because that failure did not exercise the BOUND, the mutation was re-aimed: the record's stated fraction ignored and the limit loosened to 0.9. The build then publishes, and the example fails on the number it is there to check -- 'a record ordering 2 m must still move the published wave by at most 0.4 of the 1.531337650552614 m forecast, which is 0.6125350602210456 m: it moved 1.3782038854973526 m'. (3) The record's own score limit dropped: 'a record ordering 29.999999999999993 display points must still move the published score by at most 12: it fell from 91 to 61'. (4) The build made to normalise the stored file to its clamps: both examples fail on 'the stored record must survive the build byte for byte'. Mutations 2 and 3 each reddened exactly one example; mutation 4 reddened both, which is correct because both carry that assertion.
falsifiability_evidence: The four mutations above ARE the falsifiability proof; there is no separate production change to break. After every revert `git diff --stat src/` was empty and `git status --short` named only this step's test file. The methodology's deletion litmus is answered by mutations 2 and 3: with either clamp weakened or gone, these tests go red.
gates_run: npm run typecheck exit 0. Full vitest 454/454 across 85 files, up from 452/85, which is exactly this step's two examples.
